issues.title: Session without context manager usage
issues.description: The rule requires all database sessions to use 'with Session(db.engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:' pattern for proper resource management, but the code creates a session without a context manager and never closes it
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
session = Session(db.engine)
row = session.scalar(stmt)
if not row:
    raise ConversationVariableNotFoundError("conversation variable not found in the database")
row.data = variable.model_dump_json()
session.commit()
issues.rule_name: SQLAlchemy Sessions Must Use Context Managers

issues.title: Database transaction commits called on every variable update instead of batched
issues.description: The ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer now calls flush() inside the loop for each updated conversation variable, rather than batching all updates and flushing once after the loop completes. This causes multiple unnecessary database commits when multiple conversation variables are updated in a single node execution, significantly degrading performance and creating database contention. The original implementation correctly tracked whether any updates occurred with the `updated_any` flag and only flushed once after all updates were queued.

issues.title: Conversation variable persistence layer registered before persistence layer causing event ordering issue
issues.description: The conversation_variable_layer is now registered before the persistence_layer in the graph engine layer stack. In event-driven architectures with layered middleware, the order of layer registration determines the order in which layers receive and process events. By registering conversation_variable_layer first, it will receive and process NodeRunSucceededEvent events before the persistence_layer has a chance to persist the node execution state. This creates a race condition where conversation variables might be updated in the database before the corresponding node execution is persisted, leading to data inconsistency if failures occur between the two operations.

issues.title: Conversation variable persistence failures are silently ignored
issues.description: The ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer calls update() without catching exceptions, relying on the graph engine's blanket exception handler which logs but continues execution. When persistence fails (e.g., database errors, ConversationVariableNotFoundError), the exception is caught by the engine's try-except in event_manager.py, logged, and execution continues. This creates silent data loss where the in-memory variable pool contains updated values but the database doesn't, causing data inconsistency. In the original implementation, these errors would fail the node execution and stop the workflow, providing clear feedback to users.

issues.title: ConversationVariable query missing tenant_id filter
issues.description: The SELECT against the tenant-scoped ConversationVariable table is filtered by id and conversation_id only, with no tenant_id predicate. This violates the requirement that tenant-scoped queries must include tenant_id scoping to prevent cross-tenant data access.
issues.rule_name: Database Queries Must Include tenant_id Scoping

issues.title: Missing return type annotation on __init__
issues.description: The __init__ method is missing an explicit return type annotation (e.g., "-> None"), which violates the requirement that all Python function definitions include type annotations for parameters and return values.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: def __init__(self, variables: dict[tuple[str, str], object] | None = None):
issues.rule_name: Python Functions Must Include Type Annotations

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30531 - feat: Add conversation variable persistence layer

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves conversation-variable persistence out of the Variable Assigner nodes (v1 and v2) and into a new GraphEngine layer, `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer`. The layer consumes `NodeRunSucceededEvent` for VARIABLE_ASSIGNER nodes, reads the `updated_variables` from process_data, and calls `ConversationVariableUpdater` for selectors under the `conversation` namespace. The updater implementation is relocated from `core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/common/impl.py` to `services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, which also removes the `extensions.ext_database` exception from the importlinter contract. The `ReadOnlyVariablePool.get` protocol changes from `(node_id, key)` to `(selector)`, and the node unit tests now assert on process_data instead of mocking the updater.

The architectural direction is sound: nodes become pure, and persistence is centralized in one place. However, the move changes failure semantics in ways the PR does not acknowledge. The node used to fail when the conversation_id was missing or the DB write failed. Now the node reports SUCCEEDED, the layer silently returns on a missing conversation_id, and any exception raised from `on_event` is caught and logged by the event manager. The updater also opens a `Session` without closing it. Together these make persistence failures easy to miss in production.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The refactor is reasonable, but it silently changes error semantics for conversation variable writes. A DB failure or a missing conversation_id now leaves the workflow reporting success while the user's variable update is lost, with only a log line as evidence. The unclosed session in the updater is a real resource leak on a per-node-execution path. Both should be fixed before merge. The test gaps are secondary but should be closed alongside the fix.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `VariableAssignerNode` v1 and v2 each built a `ConversationVariableUpdater` (via `conversation_variable_updater_factory`) and wrote conversation variables synchronously inside `_run()`, before returning `NodeRunResult`. The workflow engine's `GraphEngine` already supports layers that observe every `GraphEngineEvent` through `EventManager._notify_layers`, so `AdvancedChatAppRunner` registers persistence layers (e.g. `PauseStatePersistenceLayer`) on the engine before running.

This PR adds `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer`, registered first in `AdvancedChatAppRunner`. When a Variable Assigner emits `NodeRunSucceededEvent`, the layer reads `updated_variables` from `process_data`, looks up each `conversation.*` selector in the runtime variable pool, and calls the updater. The updater's implementation moved to `services/`, which keeps DB access out of `core.workflow`. Nodes no longer know about the database, but they also no longer know whether persistence succeeded.
steps: Entry point: `AdvancedChatAppRunner` builds a `WorkflowEntry` and attaches layers to `graph_engine`. The new `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer` is attached before `PauseStatePersistenceLayer`.

Variable Assigner v1/v2 no longer touch the DB. They write the new value into the variable pool and report the changed variables through `process_data` via `common_helpers.variable_to_processed_data`.
When the node completes, the engine emits `NodeRunSucceededEvent`. `EventManager._notify_layers` dispatches it to each layer, and exceptions from `on_event` are caught and logged, not propagated.

The new layer filters for VARIABLE_ASSIGNER events, reads the conversation_id from `system_variable`, resolves each selector against the pool, and calls `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl.update`. Note the early return when conversation_id is None.

`ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl` (now in `services/conversation_variable_updater.py`) loads the `ConversationVariable` row by id and conversation_id, writes `variable.model_dump_json()`, and commits. The session is never closed.
`ConversationService` also imports the same factory, so the updater is shared by the service layer and the runner.

findings.title: Conversation variable DB failures are swallowed and the node still reports success
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py`, the `update()`/`flush()` calls at lines 52-53 run inside `on_event`. The event manager (`api/core/workflow/graph_engine/event_management/event_manager.py`, `_notify_layers`) catches and logs any exception from `on_event`, so a failed DB write (`ConversationVariableNotFoundError` or a SQLAlchemy error) is silently dropped while the node has already reported SUCCEEDED. Restore the previous guarantee that a failed conversation-variable write fails the run. Either persist from the node again, or have the layer surface the failure, for example by sending a command through `self.command_channel` that aborts the graph or by recording an error the engine checks. Keep the layer's responsibility narrow and add a test that a raising updater produces a visible failure.

findings.title: Missing conversation_id now silently skips persistence instead of failing
findings.body:
The old v1 node raised `VariableOperatorNodeError("conversation_id not found")` when `sys.conversation_id` was missing. The old v2 node raised `ConversationIDNotFoundError` unless `invoke_from == DEBUGGER`. The new layer returns silently in both cases.

The effect is that a non-debugger chat run that somehow lacks a conversation_id will update the in-memory conversation variable, report success, and never persist it. The v2 exception was also the only place that enforced the DEBUGGER exemption, and the layer has no equivalent check. `if conversation_id is None` also lets an empty string through, while the old v1 code used `if not conversation_id`.

::diff{file="api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py" lines="34-36"}

If the debugger case is intentional, make it explicit (for example, only skip when `invoke_from == DEBUGGER`, which the layer can read from the system variables or a constructor flag). For any other missing id, fail the run rather than dropping the write.
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` lines 34-36, the layer returns silently when `system_variable.conversation_id` is None. Before this PR, the v1 assigner raised `VariableOperatorNodeError` on a missing conversation_id, and the v2 assigner raised `ConversationIDNotFoundError` unless `invoke_from == InvokeFrom.DEBUGGER` (see the removed block in `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/node.py`). Restore that behaviour: skip only for the debugger case, and otherwise raise or surface an error so the write is not silently dropped. Use `not conversation_id` in place of `is None` to match the old v1 check. Add unit tests for the None and empty-string cases.

findings.title: Database session opened without a context manager and never closed
findings.body:
The original `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl.update` used `with Session(db.engine) as session:`, which closes the session on exit. The move to `services/conversation_variable_updater.py` changed this to a bare `session = Session(db.engine)`. Nothing closes the session on the success path or on the `ConversationVariableNotFoundError` raise path.

The layer calls `update()` once per conversation variable per assigner node. In a long chat workflow, each call leaks a pooled connection until garbage collection runs. Under load that can exhaust the SQLAlchemy pool. The `commit()` also happens on a session that may still hold a transaction if the commit raises.

::diff{file="api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py" lines="18-23"}

Restore the context manager, which keeps the cleanup on the exception path too.

::suggestion{file="api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py" lines="18-23"}
with Session(db.engine) as session:
    row = session.scalar(stmt)
    if not row:
        raise ConversationVariableNotFoundError("conversation variable not found in the database")
    row.data = variable.model_dump_json()
    session.commit()
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl.update` (lines 18-23) creates `session = Session(db.engine)` without closing it. This leaks a DB connection on every call, including the not-found raise path. Restore the original `with Session(db.engine) as session:` block that the previous version of `core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/common/impl.py` used, and keep the `scalar`, not-found check, `row.data` assignment, and `commit()` inside it. Keep the new `ConversationVariableNotFoundError` type.

findings.title: Unit tests miss the new error and edge branches in the persistence layer
findings.body:
The four new layer tests cover the happy path, missing outputs, a non-assigner node, and a non-conversation selector. None of the following branches are exercised:

- `conversation_id is None` (the silent-skip path discussed above)
- a selector with `len < 2` (the warning path)
- a conversation selector that is missing from the variable pool (the warning path)
- an updater that raises. This matters most, because it is exactly the failure that is now silently dropped.

The node-level tests were also changed to stop asserting on the DB write, and nothing in the test suite checks that `AdvancedChatAppRunner` registers the layer. A regression that removes the `graph_engine.layer(conversation_variable_layer)` line would not fail any test.

::diff{file="api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py" lines="38-51"}

Add tests for each branch above, and assert the expected observable outcome: whether `update` was called, and whether the failure is surfaced.
findings.fixPrompt: Extend `api/tests/unit_tests/core/app/layers/test_conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` to cover the untested branches in `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py`: (1) conversation_id None and empty string, (2) selectors shorter than 2, (3) a conversation selector that is missing from the pool, (4) an updater whose `update` raises. For each one, assert the observable result (updater call or not, and whether the error propagates or is surfaced). Keep the existing `Mock(spec=...)` style and helper functions. Once the layer's failure semantics are settled, assert that they hold.

findings.title: Dead exception and redundant constructor left behind in Variable Assigner v2
findings.body:
After this change, `ConversationIDNotFoundError` in `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/exc.py` has no raisers or importers. Its only use was the block that was removed from v2's `_run`. Leaving it defined suggests the check still exists somewhere.

The new `__init__` added to `VariableAssignerNode` v2 only forwards the same four arguments to `super().__init__`. It adds nothing and can be deleted, since the base class constructor already has this signature.

::diff{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/node.py" lines="193-197"}

Remove the unused exception class (or its import, if it is re-exported) and the redundant constructor.
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/node.py`, the `__init__` added to `VariableAssignerNode` only forwards its arguments to `super().__init__` and can be removed. In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/exc.py`, `ConversationIDNotFoundError` is no longer raised or imported anywhere after this PR, so delete it, after confirming with grep that no other module references it. Keep the rest of the exc module unchanged.

findings.title: Protocol and boundary changes are consistent across the codebase
findings.body: Moving the updater into `services/` is the right call. It removes the `extensions.ext_database` exception from the importlinter contract, so `core.workflow` no longer depends on the database layer. The old `common/impl.py` has no remaining importers. The `ReadOnlyVariablePool.get` signature change from `(node_id, key)` to `(selector, /)` is applied in the protocol, the wrapper, and the pause-state test mock. I searched for two-argument `get` callers and found none in the source. Keeping the test mock's `get(selector)` consistent with the protocol is a good sign that the change was made deliberately.

findings.title: Node-level tests now verify the emitted event rather than mocked DB writes
findings.body: The v1 node tests drop the `mock.Mock(spec=ConversationVariableUpdater)` assertions and check the `NodeRunSucceededEvent` payload through `common_helpers.get_updated_variables`. This moves the assertion to observable output, which is the right boundary now that the node no longer writes to the DB. Those tests will survive future refactors of the persistence path better than mock call-count assertions did.
